fields.v: Díaz, J., Pérez, J., Gil-Borrás, S. (2026). Methodological Harness in Agentic Software Engineering: An Empirical Study on Mining Software Repositories. arXiv:2609.32014v1 [cs.SE], 25 Sep 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2609.32014v1 [cs.SE], 25 Sep 2026; no venue or submission stated
Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, Spain (all three authors)

Evaluates — repository mining: descriptive study of whether the authors' methodological harness framework is observable in 5,435 GitHub repositories with agentic PRs from AIDev (RQ1 adoption of mechanisms, RQ2 content of 285 rule files). No agent run; effects not measured

Methodological harness framework (Díaz et al. 2026, the authors' prior multivocal-review-based framework, linked to SDD): eight mechanisms H1 context engineering, H2 persistent shared knowledge, H3 executable specifications, H4 N-version mindset and parallel agents, H5 normative specifications, H6 structured consultation, H7 evidence-based acceptance, H8 graduated autonomy; no version. Spec Kit paths (.specify/specs, .specify/memory) used as detector patterns

Rule/context files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .cursor/rules, .windsurfrules, .clinerules, copilot-instructions.md) for H1/H5; ADRs and .specify/memory for H2; executable specifications (specs/**, .specify/specs/**, Gherkin *.feature, openapi.{yaml,json}) for H3; PR templates (H7); CODEOWNERS (H8); structured consultation records in PR comments (H6). Specifications described as the central coordination substrate

Not stated as a sequential flow; mechanisms grouped into three functions: knowledge management, production support, governance (Fig. 1). Framework intends them to operate as a coherent system (executable specs enable evidence-based acceptance, etc.)

Prescribed by the framework: structured consultation (agent suspends and asks a human, H6), evidence-based acceptance bundle (H7), graduated autonomy deciding when human planning, approval or review is required (H8), CODEOWNERS reviewers
Not run; artefacts detected in repositories (document/repository-based): path and lexical detectors for 7 of 8 mechanisms (H4 excluded); manual coding of 285 rule files from 150 repositories
Not classifiable (adoption study; framework 'linked to SDD' with specifications as coordination substrate, no Böckeler level stated); authors use "specification-driven development (SDD)"
Existing code bases (GitHub repositories with agent-created PRs, AIDev dataset); no development task is run
fields.why: Mining study: no task is given to an agent, so the field could equally be N/A
fields.doubt: Estudo de mineração: nenhum agente executa tarefas. Decide se o tipo de tarefa fica 'existing code base' (repositórios do AIDev) ou N/A.

Differential attrition in lowest stratum; H6 lexical detector failed (recall 0.49); canonical-name detectors give lower bounds; H2 may be invisible (external memory services); early-adopter bias; H5 detector English-only; no outcome variables, no efficacy claims. Future: effect of the harness with pre-registered outcome study; team size measure; cumulative incidence analysis; practitioner study for H2

Yes (1): Wilson CIs, reweighting, sensitivity analyses (stub files, single-PR repos, language), inter-coder reliability
fields.why: The authors deliberately do no significance testing (p. 7); variability is handled with 95% Wilson intervals, reweighting and sensitivity analyses (pp. 23, 29-30). Yes or Partly depends on whether CIs without tests of differences count as 'statistical analysis of differences'
fields.doubt: Os autores recusam testes de significância e usam só intervalos de Wilson e análises de sensibilidade (pp. 7, 23, 29-30). Decide se isto vale Yes ou Partly.
